neighbours.label: comparison word in an arithmetic word problem ('more ... than', 'less than', 'times as many')
fire: A farmer has 45 sheep, which is 12 more than the number of goats he owns.
Tom's sister is 8 years younger than Tom, who is 20 years old.
There are three times as many red marbles as blue marbles in the jar.
The second train travels 15 miles per hour slower than the first one.
Anna saved 30% less money this month than she did last month.
A pen costs 2 dollars more than a pencil, and together they cost 3 dollars.
The rectangle's length is twice its width, and its perimeter is 36 cm.
Jake read 40 fewer pages than Maria, who read 150 pages.
quiet: A farmer has 45 sheep and 33 goats on his small farm by the river.
Tom's sister is 12 years old, and Tom is 20 years old.
There are 18 red marbles and 6 blue marbles in the jar.
The second train travels at 45 miles per hour toward the city.
Anna saved 210 dollars this month and 300 dollars last month.
A pen costs 2.50 dollars and a pencil costs 0.50 dollars.
The rectangle has a width of 6 cm and a perimeter of 36 cm.
Jake read 110 pages, and Maria read 150 pages this week.

notes: card: weak pole (max 3.7, 82% gate-closed echo); top two examples are 'less' and 'than' in math word problems, others are numbers and separators. Near misses: same problems stated without a comparison.
